$comment: C12 — the host registry for `scripts/install-agent-rules.mjs` and the rule set for
`scripts/skills-portability-audit.mjs`.
WHY A CONTRACT AND NOT A CONST IN THE SCRIPT. The conventions system (skills/conventions)
learned this the hard way: a hardcoded list of conventions goes stale the day someone adds
a snippet, so the skill is told to Glob the directory instead. Hosts cannot be globbed —
they are external products — so the list has to be written down somewhere. Writing it HERE
rather than in the installer means (a) the installer has no host knowledge of its own and
cannot drift from this file, (b) `provenance` can travel next to each path, and (c) the
audit and the installer read the SAME declaration of what a portable skill looks like.
PROVENANCE IS PART OF THE DATA. Four of these products are not installed as libraries we
can interrogate; their rule paths are documentation claims. Every target therefore carries
how its path was established, and the installer PRINTS that in the preview. A user is
entitled to know which of the seven targets was empirically confirmed on this machine and
which is being taken on a vendor's word.
THE NEIGHBOUR THIS FILE EXISTS TO AVOID. `<repo>/.codex/config.toml` is gitignored and
holds a live bearer token; a deny-list build once shipped it inside a .mcpb (see
contracts/export-allowlist.json). Three properties, stated as narrowly as they hold:
every target file name is CONSTRUCTED by joining a base with a `file` fragment from this
contract, so no path comes from user input; `allowedTargetExtensions` and the declared
basenames are re-checked on the resolved path before any open, so a `.toml` this contract
cannot name the installer cannot name either; and a target that is itself a symlink is
refused rather than followed. That last check covers the FINAL COMPONENT ONLY — a reparse
point on a parent directory still redirects the write, and the lstat/rename window is not
closed. The claim that holds is 'no code path names a file this contract does not name, and
a target that is a link is refused', NOT 'the process cannot read' and NOT 'name and inode
cannot diverge'. The wider claims would be false, and a false security claim is worse than none.

block.name: skills-index
$comment: Same HTML-comment marker shape as `installGlobalConvention()` in scripts/setup-vault.mjs
(v0.13.9), and for the same reason: these files are flat documents a human also writes in.
A marker block lets us own our paragraphs, re-render them on upgrade, and leave every other
line alone. A BEGIN with no matching END is an ambiguous state and is REFUSED, never guessed.
The Agent Skills spec admits exactly six frontmatter keys. Claude Code accepts many more
and drops the extras; the spec distribution paths (claude.ai upload, the Skills API,
package_skill.py) FAIL HARD on an extra key rather than ignoring it. So a key outside this
set is not a style question — it decides whether the skill can leave Claude Code at all.
$authorityNote: WHICH DOCUMENT IS THE AUTHORITY, AND WHY IT MATTERS. Two numbers were in play and they
are not the same measurement. https://agentskills.io/specification — the open Agent Skills
spec, which is what a NON-Claude host validates against — states verbatim, in its
frontmatter table: `description` | Yes | 'Max 1024 characters. Non-empty. Describes what
the skill does and when to use it.' and, under the `description` field heading, 'Must be
1-1024 characters'. The 1,536 figure comes from the Claude Code docs and is a different
thing entirely: the point at which the combined `description` + `when_to_use` text is
TRUNCATED IN CLAUDE CODE'S SKILL LISTING. A truncation threshold in one host is not a
This audit exists to answer 'could this page leave Claude Code unedited?', so the open
spec is the authority and 1024 is the limit. Pinning the wrong one was not cosmetic: at
1536 the audit reported 0 errors over 47 skills, when 3 of them were in fact invalid.
portableFrontmatter.budgetSource: https://agentskills.io/specification (accessed 2026-08-08) — `description`: 'Must be 1-1024 characters'; `compatibility`: 'Must be 1-500 characters if provided'; `name`: 'Must be 1-64 characters'.

claudeCodeListingTruncation.$note: Recorded, deliberately NOT enforced as a spec rule. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (accessed 2026-08-08): the combined `description` + `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing. It is a host display budget, looser than the spec limit above, so the spec limit binds first and this number never decides a verdict.

portableFrontmatter.$namePatternNote: Encodes all four of the spec's name rules at once: lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens only, no leading hyphen, no trailing hyphen, no consecutive hyphens (the alternation cannot produce `--`).

argument-hint.reason: Autocomplete hint for the slash-command form. This repo's shipping path is the Claude Code plugin, where every documented field is legal, so the key earns its place there. It is recorded here — rather than deleted or ignored — because it is exactly the key the upstream docs use to illustrate the hard error ('Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter: argument-hint'), so any skill carrying it cannot be lifted onto a spec distribution path unedited. `--strict` promotes this to an error and prints the list.

agents-md.label: AGENTS.md (portable — read by Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Windsurf)

project.source: https://agents.md/ — open format, repository root, nested files allowed; the site lists OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Windsurf among its readers.
project.note: One file, four hosts. Install this first; the host-specific targets below are for the cases where a host is driven from OUTSIDE a project that has an AGENTS.md.

user.source: Codex reads AGENTS.md; the user-scope copy lives under CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex), the same root `codex exec -p` layers profile config from.
user.note: CODEX_HOME is honoured when set — that is also what keeps the test suite off the real ~/.codex.

user.source: Gemini CLI hierarchical context loading — global context file at ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md, applied to every project.
user.note: GEMINI.md, not AGENTS.md: the global tier is keyed on the context file name, which defaults to GEMINI.md.

project.source: Same: project-level context files are discovered in the workspace directory and its parents.
https://cursor.com/docs/context/rules — project rules live in .cursor/rules as .mdc files, version-controlled; frontmatter keys are description, globs, alwaysApply.

frontmatter.description: obsidian-mcp-router — index of the vault know-how skills and where to read each one. Consult when working with an Obsidian vault, the router's MCP tools, or any wiki ingestion, linting or export task.

$frontmatterNote: `description`, `globs` and `alwaysApply`, and the activation policy is chosen from them.
ACTIVATION IS DELIBERATE, and the earlier `alwaysApply: false` with no `globs` was the
one combination that makes the file inert: with no globs to match and no always-on
flag, the rule waits to be fetched by description alone, which is precisely the
chicken-and-egg this index exists to break — an agent cannot ask for the catalogue of
skills it does not know about. An index is exactly the kind of always-loaded, cheap
pointer list `alwaysApply` is for; the expensive pages stay behind it, loaded on demand.
`globs` is empty because the index is not file-scoped.
project.note: No user-scope target: Cursor's User Rules are edited in Customize -> Rules and the docs publish no filesystem path for them. Guessing one would be a write into an unknown location, so the host is project-scope only.

project.source: Windsurf Rules — workspace rules under .windsurf/rules/*.md (legacy fallback path, still read), 12,000 characters per file.
project.note: The docs now name .devin/rules/*.md as preferred with .windsurf/rules/*.md as the legacy fallback. This contract writes the legacy path because it is the one the spec for this work named and the one the installed product still reads; moving it is a one-line change here, which is the point of putting it here.

user.note: The tightest budget of the seven targets, and the reason the renderer has a compact mode at all. A file that overflows its budget is REFUSED with `over-budget`, never silently truncated — a half-written index is worse than no index, because the missing half looks like a skill that does not exist.

project.description: The project directory the installer was pointed at (--project, default: cwd).
